 Judgment

01. This review petition has been filed under Section 65 of the J&K High Court Rules, 1999 read with Order 47 Rule 1 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 seeking review of judgment dated 12.03.2024 delivered by this Court by a common judgment passed in MA No. 193/2010 titled - "New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs Shakti Devi & Ors.".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
02. It has been asserted in the review petition that there is an error apparent on the face of the record which has crept in the judgment passed in MA No. 193/2010 as it appears that inadvertently in said appeal the deceased was taken as a bachelor and 50% of his income for personal expenses was deducted instead of 1/3rd deducted by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kishtwar [in short,
"the Tribunal''] to compute the compensation whereas the fact of the matter was that the deceased was a married person having children and the deduction on account of personal expenses should have been 1/3rd instead of 50% as was taken by this Court.
Shakti Devi Age 70 Years vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56617558/
1 03.

It has also been contended that the judgment sought to be reviewed had not taken into account the enhancement under the head future prospects which the claimants were entitled to the extent of 40% having regard to their age in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the judgments titled as "Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Ors." and "National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Pranay Sethi".
04.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the review petitioners argued that on both these counts, the judgment passed by this Court is required to be reviewed making corrections which are apparent on the face of the record.

He has further argued that so far as deduction on personal expenses is concerned, the Tribunal had deducted 1/3rd of the income on the personal expenses but this court inadvertently treated deceased as bachelor while computing the compensation and had deducted 50% of his income on his personal expenses.
05. He has also argued that though the Tribunal had not stepped up the income of the deceased by 40% and the claimants had also not filed an appeal.

However, this Court while exercising the appellate jurisdiction could have exercised its powers to enhance the income of the deceased to workout the loss of future income in view of the settled law laid down having precedents by the Apex Court in the judgments "Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Ors."
and "National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Pranay Sethi".
06.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He has finally submitted that the judgment dated 12.03.2024 passed by this Court be reviewed and the compensation to which the claimants were entitled be worked out having regard to the deduction of 1/3rd income on personal expenses of the deceased and stepping up his income by 40%
for calculation of the future loss of income.

07. Learned counsel for the respondent, on the other hand, while rebutting the arguments raised by the learned counsel for the review petitioners submitted that the review petitioners cannot seek enhancement of the compensation by applying the stepping up of the income as they had not filed any appeal against the award passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Kishtwar and once the award was not challenged by them it can be safely held that they were satisfied with the award, as such, in this review petition they cannot be allowed to set up a new case altogether to seek enhanced compensation.
08. He, however, has admitted that the deceased in this case was a married person and not a bachelor as was accepted by this Court and on that count instead of 50% deduction of the income

,
1/3rd of the income should have been deducted for computation of the compensation.

09. So far as, the 1st contention with regard to deduction on personal expenses is concerned as admitted by the other side and also as was the case accepted by the Tribunal that the deceased in the case was a married person, as such, having regard to the number of dependants as three, 1/3rd deduction of his personal expenses on his personal account should have been made.
Therefore, to that extent, there is an error apparent on the face of the record which is required to be corrected.

sentences.text: The 2nd contention with regard to stepping up of the income of the deceased by 40% in the case is concerned, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in various judgments particularly in "Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Ors." reported as 2018 Legal Eagle (SC) 786 and "National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Pranay Sethi" reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680 observed that having regard to the future prospects of increase in income, in case of self-employed as the deceased was in this case, up to the age of 40 years and addition of 40% of the established income should be granted towards future prospects.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Ors." reported as 2018 Legal Eagle (SC) 786
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Pranay Sethi" reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These judgments passed by the Apex Court ought to be followed by the High Courts and the Tribunals as a legal precedent and cannot be deviated.
Therefore, on this count also, the judgment is required to be reviewed to correct the error apparent on the face of the record.

11. When a case is decided, the Court considers the claim and the relief sought applies the statute which is applicable and the law which is laid down particularly when it is by a Constitutional Bench in deciding the case just as in the case of a judgment where the applicable statute not being applied would result in a judgment which becomes amenable to be corrected and reviewed

, when a binding judgment of Supreme Court which is enlisted by the parties ignored it should not have a different consequence, in fact, the power of review is to be exercised based on provision of Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Any such refusal to follow the decision binding on it would undoubtedly disclose an error which would be palpable being self-evident.

12. So far as the contention of the learned counsel for the respondent that since the claimants have not filed the appeal themselves, their plea to seek modification in the quantum of compensation cannot be entertained by this Court in an appeal filed by the appellant/insurer.

This question is no longer res Integra in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled "Jitendra Khimshankar Trivedi & Ors. v. Kasam Daud Kumbhar & Ors.", reported as (2015) 4 SCC 237, wherein it has been held that even if the claimant did not challenge the award passed by the Tribunal, the Courts are obliged to award just and reasonable compensation even by increasing the compensation.

entities.text: Jitendra Khimshankar Trivedi & Ors. v. Kasam Daud Kumbhar & Ors.", reported as (2015) 4 SCC 237
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Paras 14 to 16 of the judgment are relevant and are extracted as under:
"14.

As against the award passed by the tribunal even though the claimants have not preferred any appeal and even though the claimants have then prayed for compensation of Rs.2,96,480/-, for doing complete justice to the parties, exercising jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, we deem it appropriate to award enhanced compensation of Rs. 6,47,000/ to the claimants.
15. In situation of this nature, for doing complete justice to the parties, this Court has always exercised the jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.

In Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs. Brij Mohan and Ors.,8 this Court 8 (2007) 7 SCC 56 held as under:-
13.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs. Brij Mohan and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, Respondent 1 is a poor labourer.
He had suffered grievous injuries.
He had become disabled to a great extent.
The amount of compensation awarded in his favour appears to be on a lower side.

In the aforementioned situation, although we reject the other contentions of Ms Indu Malhotra, we are inclined to exercise our Shakti Devi Age 70 Years vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56617558/
3 extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India so as to direct that the award may be satisfied by the appellant but it would be entitled to realise the same from the owner of the tractor and the trolley wherefor it would not be necessary for it to initiate any separate proceedings for recovery of the amount as provided for under the Motor Vehicles Act.
14.

entities.text: Shakti Devi Age 70 Years vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well settled that in a situation of this nature this Court in exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India read with Article 136 thereof can issue suit directions for doing complete justice to the parties".

16. In Deddappa & Ors. vs. Branch Manager, National Insurance Company Limited,9 it was observed as under:-
"26.

entities.text: Deddappa & Ors. vs. Branch Manager, National Insurance Company Limited,9
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, as the appellant hails from the lowest strata of society, we are of the opinion that in a case of this nature, we should, in exercise of our extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, direct Respondent 1 to pay the amount of claim to the appellants herein and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle viz. Respondent 2, particularly in view of the fact that no appeal was preferred by him.
We direct accordingly".

Therefore, the contention raised by learned counsel for the appellant with regard to the fact that this Court while exercising the appellate jurisdiction cannot entertain the plea of the respondent-claimant to seek modification of the quantum of compensation is not tenable and is hereby rejected.
13.
Having regard to the aforesaid reasons and discussions made hereinabove, the judgment is reviewed and the compensation is worked out as follows:-

"After stepping up of the annual income which had been fixed as 40,000/- by the Tribunal, by 40% (i.e. Rs. 16,000/-), the annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.
56,000/- but after deducting 1/3rd of this income on personal expenses, the annual loss of dependency comes to Rs. 39,334/- and after applying the multiplier of 17 having regard to the age of the deceased, the total loss of dependency comes to Rs.
6,68,678/-."
14.

Therefore, the loss of dependency to the claimants is modified from Rs. 3,40,000/- to Rs.
6,68,678/-
The compensation granting under rest of the heads is, however, maintained as granted by the Tribunal.

The total compensation, thus, is modified as per the following details:-
1. Loss of Dependency Rs. 6,68,678/-
2. Loss of Estate Rs. 5,000/-
3. Cremation expenses Rs. 2,000/-

sentences.text: 4. Loss of consortium Rs. 5,000/-

15. The 3rd contention of the learned counsel for the review petitioners is that the interest of 9% should have been granted.
However, this plea cannot be accepted for the reason that there is no 'straight jacket formula' for grant of compensation and the rate of interest granted by the Tribunal shall be maintained.
16. The present review petition is, accordingly, disposed of as allowed.
(M A CHOWDHARY) JUDGE JAMMU 13.09.2024
